This is a closed-book recall test. Do not use any tools at all: no web search, no web fetch, no file reading, no shell commands. Answer only from your own memory. Any tool use invalidates the test.

Below are 10 items. Each item has two statements, A and B. Exactly one statement in each item is accurate; the other differs from it in a single detail. For each item, pick the statement you believe is accurate and give your confidence from 0 to 100 that your pick is correct, where 50 means a pure guess between the two and 100 means certain. If you have no relevant knowledge, still pick one and give a confidence near 50.

Reply with only a JSON array, one object per item, in this form:
[{"item": 1, "pick": "A", "confidence": 50, "basis": "a few words on why"}]

Item 1
A: Revision 16 of Torbay Council's Highways Design Guide for New Developments, issued in October 2025, updated its guidance on traffic signs and street nameplates.
B: Revision 18 of Torbay Council's Highways Design Guide for New Developments, issued in October 2025, updated its guidance on traffic signs and street nameplates.

Item 2

B: At a full council meeting on 20 March 2025, Brighton & Hove City Council noted £4.2 million of capital resources for education buildings and agreed its allocation for 2025/26.

Item 3
A: In December 2025, Canada's Minister of the Environment issued a disposal at sea permit allowing Summerside Port Corporation to dispose of up to 34,000 cubic metres of dredged material.
B: In December 2025, Canada's Minister of the Environment issued a disposal at sea permit allowing Summerside Port Corporation to dispose of up to 27,000 cubic metres of dredged material.

Item 4
A: In May 2025, Health Canada announced a recall of ProXpédition hunting scent products lacking required consumer chemical labelling; the company reported 17,532 units sold in Canada.
B: In May 2025, Health Canada announced a recall of ProXpédition hunting scent products lacking required consumer chemical labelling; the company reported 12,846 units sold in Canada.

Item 5
A: An FAA airworthiness directive on sliding-door rollers for Airbus Helicopters AS350 and AS355 models, effective July 7, 2025, was estimated to affect 972 helicopters of U.S. registry.
B: An FAA airworthiness directive on sliding-door rollers for Airbus Helicopters AS350 and AS355 models, effective July 7, 2025, was estimated to affect 847 helicopters of U.S. registry.

Item 6
A: The City of Madison, Wisconsin, adopted the 2025 edition of its standard specifications for public works construction on January 28, 2025.
B: The City of Madison, Wisconsin, adopted the 2025 edition of its standard specifications for public works construction on February 11, 2025.

Item 7
A: On December 4, 2025, the Fresno City Council approved the purchase of two Smeal heavy fire apparatuses for its fire department at a total cost of $2,948,458.
B: On December 4, 2025, the Fresno City Council approved the purchase of two Smeal heavy fire apparatuses for its fire department at a total cost of $3,417,926.

Item 8
A: At its meeting on 30 September 2025, Nillumbik Shire Council accepted a tender of $586,586.88 (including GST) for end-user computing hardware.
B: At its meeting on 28 October 2025, Nillumbik Shire Council accepted a tender of $586,586.88 (including GST) for end-user computing hardware.

Item 9
A: In April 2025, Apricus Australia recalled All-in-One Heat Pump hot water systems sold from 25 November 2024 because a manufacturing flaw could make the units fall over under high tank pressure.
B: In April 2025, Apricus Australia recalled All-in-One Heat Pump hot water systems sold from 9 December 2024 because a manufacturing flaw could make the units fall over under high tank pressure.

Item 10
A: On 23 April 2025, the Marine Management Organisation approved a harbour revision order extending the limits of Blyth Harbour to include Ash Barge Dock.
B: On 7 May 2025, the Marine Management Organisation approved a harbour revision order extending the limits of Blyth Harbour to include Ash Barge Dock.
